## Using this analysis companion {#using-this-companion}

We jointly estimated baseline ornament expression and post-breeding molt midpoint from repeated photographs of marked banded dotterels. We first compared sex, age class and migratory status. We then examined breeding-related plasticity in confidently after-first-year birds by separating differences among individuals from seasonal changes within the same birds. Throughout, **adult includes both first-year and after-first-year birds**. We use AFY specifically for the after-first-year sample.

### Render the completed analyses

1. Keep the repository folders together and open R in the project root, which contains this `.qmd` file.
2. Install the packages listed under [Reproducibility details](#reproducibility-details). The setup chunk checks for missing packages before loading data.
3. Render with Quarto from the project root:

```{.bash}
quarto render banded_dotterel_moult.qmd --to html
```

Rendering reads the completed model objects in `out/`. **No model is fitted when the document is rendered.** Model-fitting chunks are displayed with `eval=FALSE`. They require `cmdstanr` and CmdStan if run manually. Expand “Show R code” beside each analysis to inspect its implementation, or use the Code menu to view the complete source.

## Data import and sample summary

We used repeated photographs from an individually marked breeding population at Kaikōura to assess variation in baseline rufous-band expression and the timing of its post-breeding replacement. The photographic dataset spans the 2021–2022, 2022–2023 and 2023–2024 breeding seasons. We linked photographs to breeding records and, where available, age class and migratory status. The following summaries distinguish raw photographic records from the distinct scored observations used in fitting.

```{r}
dat_breeding <-
  readRDS(
    here("data/moult_breeding_KK_data.rds")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rings_comb_raw = as.character(rings_comb),
    rings_comb = rings_comb_simp
  )

# Use one season-specific centering/scaling rule throughout the qmd so
# t0 and k remain comparable across model subsets.
date_scaling_ref <- dat_breeding %>%
  distinct(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(
    date_J_mean_ref = mean(date_J, na.rm = TRUE),
    date_J_sd_ref = sd(date_J, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

add_reference_date_scaling <- function(data, date_col = "date_J") {
  data %>%
    left_join(date_scaling_ref, by = "season") %>%
    mutate(
      date_J_scaled = (.data[[date_col]] - date_J_mean_ref) / date_J_sd_ref
    )
}
```

For all analyses below, `rings_comb` is the simplified individual identifier (`rings_comb_simp`), while the original raw notation is retained as `rings_comb_raw`. This collapses duplicated raw codes such as `RBLY`/`RBLY_F`, `RBYG`/`RBYG_F`, and `RRYY`/`RRYY_F` to the same biological individual.

We first summarise the number of photographs and the date range covered
in each season.

```{r, echo= FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(n_obs = n(),
            min_date = min(date),
            max_date = max(date))
```

We then count the number of individuals represented in the full
photographic dataset.
```{r, echo = FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  pull(rings_comb) %>% unique() %>% length()
```

Finally, we check how many individuals were sampled in more than one
season, because repeated sampling across years is what allows us to
estimate persistent individual differences.
```{r, echo = FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame() %>%
  select(rings_comb, season) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(rings_comb) %>%
  summarise(n_seasons = n()) %>%
  group_by(n_seasons) %>%
  summarise(n())
```

Total, mean and standard deviation of distinct scored observations per bird-season:
```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame() %>%
  group_by(rings_comb, season) %>%
  summarise(n_photos = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(total_photo = sum(n_photos),
         mean_photos_per_ind_per_season = mean(n_photos),
         sd_photos_per_ind_per_season = sd(n_photos)) %>%
  distinct(total_photo, mean_photos_per_ind_per_season, sd_photos_per_ind_per_season)
```

Maximum and minimum numbers of distinct scored observations per bird-season:
```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame() %>%
  group_by(rings_comb, season) %>%
  summarise(n_photos = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(sum_n = sum(n_photos),
         mean_n = mean(n_photos),
         sd_n = sd(n_photos)) %>%
  summarise(max_photos_ind_season = max(n_photos),
            min_photos_ind_season = min(n_photos))
```

### Table of scored photos
The table below retains the raw photographic records. For fitting, we collapse records with identical bird, date, score, sex and season values, then remove missing values required by the model. Different scores on the same date are not automatically collapsed. The full sex-specific model contains 1,646 distinct scored observations, whereas the existing raw-data plotting layers contain 2,285 records. Reconciliation of those plotting layers is deferred.

#### Variable definitions

- <code>sourcefile</code>: the original photograph path in the catalogue
- <code>rings_comb_raw</code>: the original 4-band code in the raw dataset, including occasional duplicate notations for the same bird
- <code>rings_comb</code>: the simplified individual identifier used throughout the analyses (`rings_comb_simp`)
- <code>score</code>: the score of the rufous breast band according to the 1-7 scheme shown below
- <code>date</code>: the date of the photo (extracted from the photo's metadata)
- <code>date_J</code>: the Julian date of the photo, shifted to span the austral summer
- <code>sex</code>: sex based on plumage (M or F)
- <code>season</code>: breeding season of the given photo
- <code>migratory_status</code>: Resident (R) or migrant (M) classified from satellite tracking and/or winter resightings
- <code>age_class</code>: FY (hatched in the previous breeding season) or AFY (known to be older from hatch histories or adult marking in an earlier season). Birds first marked as adults have unknown age class in that season unless hatch history establishes it.
- <code>age_class_source</code>: the evidence used for assigning age class
- <code>age</code>: known age in years at the time of the photo (only available for those that were banded locally as chicks and recruited)
- <code>first_date_breeding_final</code>: first recorded incubation or brood-care date, consolidated from field visits and nest records (raw date)
- <code>last_date_breeding_final</code>: last recorded incubation or brood-care date, consolidated from field visits and nest records (raw date)
- <code>last_nest_first_obs</code>: last nest date, combining an earlier estimated laying date when available with first observation otherwise (raw date)
- <code>first_breeding_date_J_snum</code>: first recorded breeding date (season-centered Julian date, shifted for austral summer)
- <code>last_breeding_date_J_snum</code>: last recorded breeding date (season-centered Julian date, shifted for austral summer)
- <code>last_nest_first_obs_J_snum</code>: last nest date (season-centered Julian date, shifted for austral summer)

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
  select(
    sourcefile, rings_comb_raw, rings_comb, score, date, date_J, sex, season, migratory_status, age,
    first_date_breeding_final, last_date_breeding_final,
    first_breeding_date_J_snum, last_breeding_date_J_snum
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(first_date_breeding_final, last_date_breeding_final),
      ~ as.Date(., origin = "1970-01-01")
    )
  ) %>%
  datatable(
    class = "cell-border stripe",
    rownames = FALSE,
    filter = "top"
  ) %>%
  formatRound(
    columns = c(
      "last_breeding_date_J_snum",
      "first_breeding_date_J_snum"
    ),
    digits = 2
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat_breeding %>%
```

### Figure S1 — raw observations by sex and season {#figure-s1}

**Figure S1.** Raw scored observations by sex and breeding season. Each row represents a color-marked bird and each point a scored observation. Within each panel, migrants appear at the top, residents in the middle and birds of unknown migratory status at the bottom. Band-combination strips are red, green and grey, respectively. Point fill indicates moult score, ranging from 1 (no rufous band) to 7 (a complete, sharply defined rufous band). Both legends appear beside each panel. Week 07 corresponds to mid-February. The date of a bird's last photograph does not identify its departure date.

## Biological questions and predictions

We compared sex, age class and migratory status as predictors of baseline ornament expression and molt midpoint (Table 1). Males were expected to express higher rufous-band scores. Shared parental care provided a basis for expecting broadly similar timing constraints between sexes, although equal participation does not establish equal reproductive costs. Earlier replacement in first-year birds could reflect age-related differences in feather wear or reproductive schedules. Departure could also constrain the schedules of migrants. These mechanisms were not measured directly.

The AFY models address a separate question about breeding-related plasticity (Table 2). Do birds with later average breeding schedules also molt later, and does the same bird shift its molt in seasons when it breeds later than usual? We examined first observed breeding date, last nest date and last observed breeding date separately. The age-class difference in midpoint and the limited linked breeding records for first-year birds motivated restricting these comparisons to confidently AFY bird-seasons. The supplementary models assess sex differences in the among- and within-individual last-breeding-date associations and in the resident–migrant contrast (Table S1).

## Nonlinear hierarchical model {#model-equations}

### Observation model and seasonal trajectory

Let $y_{ist}$ denote the rufous-band score of bird $i$ in season $s$ at photographic observation $t$. We treated the seven-point scores as a continuous response with Gaussian observation error:

$$
y_{ist}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{ist},\sigma^2). \qquad\text{(1)}
$$

We jointly estimated baseline expression, $\beta_{is}$, and the midpoint of its post-breeding decline, $t_{0,is}$:

$$
\mu_{ist}=1+(\beta_{is}-1)
\left(1-\frac{1}{1+\exp[-k(z_{ist}-t_{0,is})]}\right). \qquad\text{(2)}
$$

Here, $z_{ist}$ is the photographic date, centered and divided by its standard deviation within season. We use $z$ for photographic date and $x$ below for breeding date to distinguish the two predictors. Expected scores decline from $\beta_{is}$ towards 1. The positive parameter $k$ controls transition steepness. Photographic coverage within individuals was insufficient to estimate covariate effects on $k$, so every model retains one shared steepness parameter. The Gaussian likelihood describes variation around the trajectory and does not impose hard bounds of 1 and 7 on observations or predictions.

The R expression is the same as equation (2), with `baseline` representing $\beta$:

```{r trajectory-equation-in-r, eval=FALSE}
# z_ist = date_J_scaled, beta_is = baseline, t_0,is = t0
mu <- 1 + (baseline - 1) *
  (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (date_J_scaled - t0))))
# family = gaussian() estimates sigma as an observation-level SD.
```

### Fixed effects and repeated observations

For baseline expression and midpoint, we included fixed effects and deviations among birds and bird-seasons:

$$
\beta_{is}=\alpha^{(\beta)}+
\mathbf{X}_{is}^{(\beta)}\boldsymbol{\gamma}^{(\beta)}+
 u_i^{(\beta)}+v_{is}^{(\beta)}, \qquad\text{(3)}
$$

$$
t_{0,is}=\alpha^{(t_0)}+
\mathbf{X}_{is}^{(t_0)}\boldsymbol{\gamma}^{(t_0)}+
 u_i^{(t_0)}+v_{is}^{(t_0)}. \qquad\text{(4)}
$$

The design vectors $\mathbf{X}$ contain the fixed effects specified for each parameter. All models include sex for baseline and midpoint, and season for midpoint. The age-class and migration models add the corresponding state to both parameters. The AFY models add breeding-date components to midpoint only. We estimated a correlation between the individual deviations in baseline and midpoint:

$$
\rho_{\beta,t_0}=\operatorname{cor}
\left(u_i^{(\beta)},u_i^{(t_0)}\right). \qquad\text{(5)}
$$

The paired individual deviations follow a zero-mean bivariate normal distribution, with covariance $\rho_{\beta,t_0}\sigma_{u,\beta}\sigma_{u,t_0}$. Bird-season deviations are zero-mean normal terms. We estimated their variances separately for the two parameters, without a bird-season correlation term.

| Mathematical term | R term | Role |
|---|---|---|
| $y_{ist}$ | `score` | Observed rufous-band score |
| $z_{ist}$ | `date_J_scaled` | Standardized photographic date |
| $\beta_{is}$ | `baseline` | Ornament expression before replacement |
| $t_{0,is}$ | `t0` | Midpoint on the standardized date scale |
| $k$ | `k ~ 1` | Shared transition steepness |
| $\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\gamma}$ | e.g., `sex + season` | Fixed effects for the named parameter |
| $u_i$ and equation (5) | `(1 | i | rings_comb)` in both parameter formulas | Correlated individual intercepts |
| $v_{is}$ | `(1 | rings_comb:season)` | Bird-season intercepts for each parameter |
| $\sigma$ | Gaussian `sigma` | Photographic-score residual SD |

The shared label `i` in the two `brms` grouping terms requests the individual correlation in equation (5). It is a grouping label in R, rather than a data column. The complete state-specific formulas are displayed below each dataset.

### Separating among- and within-individual breeding associations

Following van de Pol and Wright (2009), we represented each retained breeding date as a bird's mean plus its seasonal deviation. We added both components to the midpoint formula:

$$
t_{0,is}=\alpha^{(t_0)}+
\mathbf{X}_{is}^{(t_0)}\boldsymbol{\gamma}^{(t_0)}+
\gamma_B\bar{x}_i+\gamma_W(x_{is}-\bar{x}_i)+
 u_i^{(t_0)}+v_{is}^{(t_0)}, \qquad\text{(6)}
$$

$$
\bar{x}_i=\frac{1}{n_i}\sum_{s\in S_i}x_{is}. \qquad\text{(7)}
$$

Here, $x_{is}$ is the stored season-centered breeding date in days, $S_i$ is the set of retained AFY seasons for bird $i$, and $n_i$ is its number of retained seasons. We calculated means after restricting the sample to confidently AFY bird-seasons, using one date per bird-season. Photographs do not receive separate weights in the calculation of a bird's mean. The original seasonal centering is retained. We did not recalculate seasonal means within the AFY subset.

The among-individual coefficient $\gamma_B$ compares birds with different average breeding schedules. The within-individual coefficient $\gamma_W$ describes the common association between a bird's seasonal deviation and its midpoint. It does not estimate a separate response slope for each bird. Birds with one AFY season have a zero deviation and contribute to the among-individual comparison. Annual variation is accounted for through both the season-centered breeding dates and the fixed season effects on midpoint.

The [AFY implementation](#afy-breeding-models) shows the complete construction of `breeding_mean_i`, `breeding_dev_is` and the corresponding `brms` formula. The contrast $\gamma_B-\gamma_W$ is calculated within each posterior draw. Comparing the two slopes directly avoids inferring a difference merely because one credible interval excludes zero and the other includes it.

### Repeatability and derived days per score

For either fitted parameter $\theta\in\{\beta,t_0\}$, adjusted repeatability was

$$
R_\theta=\frac{\sigma^2_{u,\theta}}
{\sigma^2_{u,\theta}+\sigma^2_{v,\theta}}.
$$

The estimates describe consistency across seasons after controlling for the fixed effects included for each parameter. Photographic-score residual variance, $\sigma^2$, describes observations around the trajectory and is excluded from these parameter-level ratios. We compare repeatabilities using paired draws of $R_\beta-R_{t_0}$. Repeatability alone does not measure plasticity in response to changes in breeding phenology.

At midpoint, the magnitude of the trajectory slope is $(\beta-1)k/4$ score units per standardized date unit. Consequently, derived days per score at midpoint are

$$
D=\frac{4d}{(\beta-1)k},
$$

where $d$ is the conversion from standardized date units to days. The reported contrasts and derived days per score use the observation-weighted mean of the original seasonal date standard deviations in the corresponding model sample. Calendar midpoints in Table 1 instead use each season's own mean and standard deviation. The AFY fits retain their reporting conversion as `midpoint_days_conversion`.

```{r parameter-summary-equations-in-r, eval=FALSE}
post <- posterior::as_draws_df(sex_mod$fitted_model)
R_baseline <- post$sd_rings_comb__baseline_Intercept^2 /
  (post$sd_rings_comb__baseline_Intercept^2 +
   post$`sd_rings_comb:season__baseline_Intercept`^2)
R_midpoint <- post$sd_rings_comb__t0_Intercept^2 /
  (post$sd_rings_comb__t0_Intercept^2 +
   post$`sd_rings_comb:season__t0_Intercept`^2)
R_difference <- R_baseline - R_midpoint
# weighted_date_scaling() is defined in the posterior-summary code below.
d <- weighted_date_scaling(sex_mod$data)$weighted_sd
female_days_per_score <- 4 * d /
  ((post$b_baseline_Intercept - 1) * post$b_k_Intercept)
```

### Date transformations and interpretation

The input `date_J` was generated as `as.numeric(format(date + 181, "%j"))` to span the austral breeding season. It is not literally the number of days since 1 July. `date_J_scaled` uses the original full sex-model reference mean and SD within each season, including in restricted samples. The breeding predictors ending in `_snum` are centered within season but remain in days. Their mean and deviation coefficients therefore represent standardized midpoint change per one-day breeding-date change before conversion to days.

The calendar-date plotting inverses in Figures 1 and 3 still require the deferred correction. Their current labels should not be used to reconstruct the season-specific calendar estimates in Table 1.

### Figure 2 — schematic of the nonlinear model {#figure-2}
```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show code of an example parameterizing the non-linear model"

# Draw a schematic version of the nonlinear curve used in all models.
# The values of beta, t0, and k are chosen for illustration only.

# Set the schematic parameters.
baseline <- 6
k <- 3.31
t0 <- 1.45

# Define the expected trajectory from the nonlinear model.
moult_mu <- function(x, baseline, k, t0) {
  1 + (baseline - 1) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (x - t0))))
}

# Build a clean x-range around the inflection point.
x <- seq(t0 - 2.5, t0 + 2.5, length.out = 600)

df <- tibble(
  x = x,
  mu = moult_mu(x, baseline = baseline, k = k, t0 = t0)
)

# At x = t0 the curve is halfway between the upper and lower asymptotes.
y_t0 <- moult_mu(t0, baseline = baseline, k = k, t0 = t0)

# The slope at t0 determines the tangent line used to illustrate k.
slope_t0 <- -(baseline - 1) * k / 4
angle_k <- atan(slope_t0) * 180 / pi

y_k <- 7
x_k <- t0 + (y_k - y_t0) / slope_t0
```

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show plotting code for the example"
fig1 <-
  ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = mu)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = baseline, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1, color = "grey70") +
  ggtext::geom_richtext(
    data = data.frame(x = min(df$x), y = baseline),
    aes(x = x, y = y - 0.1),
    label = "baseline (<span style='font-style:italic;'>β</span>)",
    family = "sans", size = 3,
    hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6,
    fill = NA, label.color = NA
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = t0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1, color = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(x = t0, y = y_t0), size = 2) +
  annotate(
    "text", size = 3,
    family = "sans",
    x = t0, y = min(df$mu),
    label = as.expression(bquote("molt midpoint" ~ "(" * italic(t)[0] * ")" == .(round(t0, 2)))),
    parse = FALSE,
    hjust = 1, vjust = 1.5, angle = 270
  ) +
  {
    slope_t0 <- -(baseline - 1) * k / 4
    geom_abline(
      intercept = y_t0 - slope_t0 * t0,
      slope = slope_t0,
      linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1, color = "grey70"
    )
  } +
  annotate(
    "text", size = 3,
    family = "sans",
    x = x_k, y = y_k,
    label = as.expression(bquote("transition steepness (" * italic(k) * ") = " * .(round(k, 2)))),
    hjust = 0.5,
    vjust = -0.5,
    angle = angle_k + 5
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 2, color = "grey30") +
  geom_point(aes(x = t0, y = y_t0), size = 5, shape = 21, fill = "white", color = "black") +
  geom_point(aes(x = -0.5, y = 6), size = 5, shape = 23, fill = "white", color = "black") +
  labs(

  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "sans"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "grey30")
  )

fig1
```

The schematic uses illustrative values $\beta=6$, $t_0=1.45$ and $k=3.31$ on the standardized date scale. They are not the current sex-model posterior medians. Replacing midpoint and steepness with the latest medians is deferred.

### Shared priors

We used $\alpha^{(\beta)}\sim\mathcal{N}(5.5,1^2)$ and zero-centered normal priors with SD 1 for other baseline coefficients. Midpoint intercept and fixed-effect coefficients received $\mathcal{N}(0,0.5^2)$ priors on the standardized photographic-date scale. We used $k\sim\mathcal{N}(1,0.5^2)$ truncated below at zero. Group-level standard deviations received exponential priors with rate 2. The baseline prior is not truncated at the score bounds. The executable `brms` definitions follow.


We use the same prior set in the main and supplementary non-linear moult models so that
differences among models reflect changes in predictors rather than
changes in prior assumptions. We define that shared prior set once here
and reuse it in each `brm()` call below.

```{r}
# Shared priors for all non-linear moult models.
moult_priors <- c(
  # The baseline score sits on the 1-7 scoring scale, so only the
  # baseline intercept is centered near the upper half of that range.
  prior(normal(5.5, 1), nlpar = "baseline", class = "b", coef = "Intercept"),
  # All non-intercept effects on baseline are treated as deviations from
  # that intercept and are therefore centered at zero.
  prior(normal(0, 1), nlpar = "baseline", class = "b"),

  # The inflection point is estimated on the season-standardized date
  # scale, so both the intercept and predictor effects are centered at zero.
  prior(normal(0, 0.5), nlpar = "t0", class = "b", coef = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 0.5), nlpar = "t0", class = "b"),

  # Positive values of k enforce the expected one-way seasonal decline.
  prior(normal(1, 0.5), nlpar = "k", lb = 0),

  # Group-level SDs are regularized, but can still be large if the data
  # support substantial heterogeneity among birds or bird-seasons.
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "baseline", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb"),
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "baseline", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb:season"),
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "t0", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb"),
  prior(exponential(2), nlpar = "t0", class = "sd", group = "rings_comb:season")
)

```

### Analysis: Sex-specific model
We first fit a model to the full dataset and asked whether males and females differed in $\beta$ and $t_0$. We used this as the reference model because sex was known for all birds and provides the full-sample estimate of baseline expression and molt timing.

#### dataset
```{r}
# wrangle data
dat_sex_mod <- dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  add_reference_date_scaling() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame()
```

#### Model formula specification

The saved model uses females as the sex reference, first-year birds as the age-class reference, and migrants as the migratory-status reference. Season 2021 denotes 2021–2022. The migration and age-class references apply only in the corresponding models. The code retains the supplied factor levels.

```{r}
mod_sex <- bf(
  score ~ 1 + (baseline - 1) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (date_J_scaled - t0)))),
  baseline ~ sex + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  t0 ~ sex + season + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  k ~ 1,
  nl = TRUE
)
```

#### fit model
```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit_mod_sex <- brm(
  formula = mod_sex,
  data = dat_sex_mod,
  family = gaussian(),
  prior = moult_priors,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 15),
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  seed = 123
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(list(fitted_model = fit_mod_sex, data = dat_sex_mod),
        file = here("out/sex_mod_.rds"))
```

### Breeding-date records and descriptive coverage {#breeding-date-records}

The complete linked-date dataset provides descriptive breeding-date ranges.
The main breeding–molt analysis and supplementary sex-by-breeding-date
interaction below use confidently AFY bird-seasons and separate among-
from within-individual associations.

#### datasets
We prepare the complete linked-breeding dataset (`dat_breeding_mod`) for
the descriptive summaries.
```{r}
# wrangle data
dat_breeding_mod <- dat_breeding %>%
  # subset to columns of interest
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season,
         last_breeding_date_J_snum,
         first_breeding_date_J_snum,
         last_nest_first_obs_J_snum) %>%
  # reduce to distinct data
  distinct() %>%
  add_reference_date_scaling() %>%
  # drop NAs
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season,
          last_breeding_date_J_snum,
          first_breeding_date_J_snum,
          last_nest_first_obs_J_snum) %>%
  # convert to dataframe
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
breeding_phenology_trait_lookup <- tibble::tribble(
  ~trait, ~date_col, ~description,
  "last_breeding_date_J_snum", "last_date_breeding_final",
  "Last breeding date",
  "first_breeding_date_J_snum", "first_date_breeding_final",
  "First breeding date",
  "last_nest_first_obs_J_snum", "last_nest_first_obs",
  "Last nest date"
)

as_breeding_date <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "Date")) {
    x
  } else {
    as.Date(x, origin = "1970-01-01")
  }
}

format_day_month <- function(x) {
  format(x, "%d %b")
}

format_season_day <- function(x) {
  ref_date <- as.Date("2001-07-01")

  if (dplyr::near(x, round(x))) {
    format_day_month(ref_date + round(x) - 1)
  } else {
    paste(
      format_day_month(ref_date + floor(x) - 1),
      format_day_month(ref_date + ceiling(x) - 1),
      sep = " / "
    )
  }
}

dat_breeding_trait_dates <- dat_breeding %>%
  semi_join(
    dat_breeding_mod %>%
      distinct(rings_comb, season),
    by = c("rings_comb", "season")
  ) %>%
  select(
    rings_comb,
    season,
    all_of(breeding_phenology_trait_lookup$date_col),
    all_of(breeding_phenology_trait_lookup$trait)
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  drop_na(all_of(breeding_phenology_trait_lookup$trait)) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(breeding_phenology_trait_lookup$date_col),
      as_breeding_date
    )
  )

breeding_phenology_summary_stats <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  breeding_phenology_trait_lookup,
  function(trait, date_col, description) {
    trait_dates <- dat_breeding_trait_dates %>%
      transmute(
        breeding_date = .data[[date_col]],
        season_day = as.integer(
          breeding_date - as.Date(paste0(as.character(season), "-07-01"))
        ) + 1
      )

    min_i <- which.min(trait_dates$season_day)
    max_i <- which.max(trait_dates$season_day)
    min_day <- trait_dates$season_day[[min_i]]
    max_day <- trait_dates$season_day[[max_i]]

    tibble(
      Trait = trait,
      Description = description,
      `n bird-seasons` = nrow(trait_dates),
      Range = paste(
        format_day_month(trait_dates$breeding_date[[min_i]]),
        format_day_month(trait_dates$breeding_date[[max_i]]),
        sep = " - "
      ),
      `Span (days)` = max_day - min_day,
      Median = format_season_day(median(trait_dates$season_day))
    )
  }
)
```

The complete-case breeding phenology dataset contained `r nrow(dat_breeding_mod)` photo observations from `r n_distinct(dat_breeding_mod$rings_comb)` individuals and `r nrow(dat_breeding_trait_dates)` bird-seasons. Because the same breeding date is repeated across photos within a bird-season, the descriptive summary below is calculated once per bird-season. Dates are reported as day-month values on the July-to-June breeding-season calendar, and the span is the difference in days between the maximum and minimum dates.

```{r, echo=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  breeding_phenology_summary_stats,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "l", "r", "l")
)
```

#### Within-individual breeding-date ranges

For birds represented in at least two seasons, we aligned month and day to a common July–June calendar and calculated each bird's latest minus earliest date. We did not subtract dates in different years directly. The table describes observed activity, rather than confirmed initiation or cessation. Unequal detection of breeding attempts can contribute to the recorded variation.

```{r within-individual-breeding-date-ranges}
within_breeding_ranges <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  breeding_phenology_trait_lookup,
  function(trait, date_col, description) {
    dat_breeding_trait_dates %>%
      transmute(rings_comb, season, date = .data[[date_col]]) %>% distinct() %>%
      mutate(common_date = as.Date(paste0(
        if_else(as.integer(format(date, "%m")) >= 7, "2001-", "2002-"),
        format(date, "%m-%d")))) %>%
      group_by(rings_comb) %>%
      summarise(n_seasons = n_distinct(season),
                range_days = as.numeric(max(common_date) - min(common_date)),
                .groups = "drop") %>%
      filter(n_seasons >= 2) %>%
      summarise(`Breeding date` = description, Birds = n(),
                `Median within-individual range (days)` = median(range_days),
                `Smallest range (days)` = min(range_days),
                `Largest range (days)` = max(range_days))
  }
)
stopifnot(all(within_breeding_ranges$Birds == 41L))
knitr::kable(within_breeding_ranges)
```

A one-day range means that the bird's earliest and latest dates differed by one day across its retained seasons. These ranges describe the full linked-breeding sample. They do not change the 47-bird AFY model sample.

#### Recorded breeding attempts

We counted distinct nest identifiers per bird-season from the three original nest-visit worksheets. We retained records of occupied nests or observed chicks, following the existing data-preparation script. The code preserves its sex-specific identifiers for reused band combinations. We then matched those records to the same 132 bird-seasons used for the breeding-date summaries.

```{r recorded-breeding-attempts}
visit_files <- c(
  "data/Kaikoura_Dotterel_2021_Feb2022_upd_Nov22_Locations.xlsx",
  "data/Kaikoura_Dotterel_Jan23_upd.xlsx",
  "data/Kaikoura_Dotterel_Feb2024_upd.xlsx"
)
visit_sheets <- c("Kaikoura_NestVisit2021_1", "Kaikoura_NestVisit_1",
                  "Kaikoura_NestVisit_1")
nest_parent_records <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(visit_files), function(j) {
  readxl::read_excel(here(visit_files[j]), sheet = visit_sheets[j],
                    col_types = "text") %>%
    filter(`Nest Status` == "Occupied" |
           as.numeric(`Number of chicks seen`) > 0 |
           as.numeric(`Number of chicks seen`) == -1) %>%
    transmute(season = as.character(2020 + j),
              nest_id = sub("^([^[:space:]]+).*", "\\1", NestID),
              parent = str_extract_all(str_remove_all(NestID, "\\|"),
                                       "\\b[Rr]\\w{3,4}\\b")) %>%
    unnest_longer(parent) %>%
    mutate(parent = toupper(parent), rings_comb = case_when(
      parent == "RROB" & season == "2021" ~ "RROB_female",
      parent == "RROB" ~ "RROB_male",
      parent == "RROW" & season == "2021" ~ "RROW_female",
      parent == "RROW" & season == "2022" ~ "RROW_male",
      TRUE ~ parent)) %>% distinct(rings_comb, season, nest_id)
}))
linked_bird_seasons <- dat_breeding_mod %>%
  distinct(rings_comb, sex, season) %>% mutate(season = as.character(season))
breeding_attempts <- nest_parent_records %>%
  inner_join(linked_bird_seasons, by = c("rings_comb", "season")) %>%
  count(rings_comb, sex, season, name = "n_attempts")
stopifnot(nrow(breeding_attempts) == 132L,
          nrow(anti_join(linked_bird_seasons, breeding_attempts,
                        by = c("rings_comb", "season"))) == 0L)
breeding_attempts %>% group_by(sex) %>%
  summarise(`Bird-seasons` = n(), `Median attempts` = median(n_attempts),
            Minimum = min(n_attempts), Maximum = max(n_attempts),
            .groups = "drop") %>% knitr::kable()
```

These counts describe recorded attempts. They do not establish that every nesting attempt was detected.

We finally tested whether migratory strategy explained variation in

## Results

Baseline ornament expression was more repeatable across seasons than molt midpoint. First-year birds reached midpoint earlier than AFY birds, while sex and migratory status showed no clear midpoint differences. The AFY breeding–molt models found positive associations with late breeding dates among birds, but no clear corresponding associations within the same individuals. The following tables summarize the saved posterior draws. The code for extracting coefficients, converting units and calculating contrasts is available beside each result.

```{r results-helpers, echo=TRUE, results="hide"}
#| code-summary: "Show posterior summaries, date conversions and table functions"
# Summarise posterior draws as a median and 95% credible interval.
summarise_posterior <- function(x) {
  tibble(
    median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    ci_lower = as.numeric(quantile(x, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)),
    ci_upper = as.numeric(quantile(x, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))
  )
}

# Format numeric intervals consistently across all reported tables.
format_numeric_interval <- function(summary_tbl, digits = 2) {
  paste0(
    round(summary_tbl$median, digits), " [",
    round(summary_tbl$ci_lower, digits), ", ",
    round(summary_tbl$ci_upper, digits), "]"
  )
}

# Convert shifted Julian dates back to the month-day labels used in the text tables.
shifted_julian_to_date <- function(x, origin_year = 2021) {
  as.Date(x - 182, origin = paste0(origin_year, "-01-01"))
}

format_shifted_julian_interval <- function(summary_tbl, digits = 2, origin_year = 2021) {
  paste0(
    sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(summary_tbl$median, origin_year), "%d %b")), " [",
    sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(summary_tbl$ci_lower, origin_year), "%d %b")), ", ",
    sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(summary_tbl$ci_upper, origin_year), "%d %b")), "]"
  )
}

# Build a summary row once the estimate has been reduced to a point estimate and interval.
summary_row_from_stats <- function(parameter, type, parameter_group, stats,
                                   digits = 2,
                                   formatter = format_numeric_interval, ...) {
  tibble(
    type = type,
    parameter_ = parameter_group,
    parameter = parameter,
    estimate = stats$median,
    ci_lower = stats$ci_lower,
    ci_upper = stats$ci_upper,
    median_CI = formatter(stats, digits = digits, ...)
  )
}

# Convenience wrapper when we start from raw posterior draws.
summary_row <- function(parameter, type, parameter_group, draws,
                        digits = 2,
                        formatter = format_numeric_interval, ...) {
  summary_row_from_stats(
    parameter = parameter,
    type = type,
    parameter_group = parameter_group,
    stats = summarise_posterior(draws),
    digits = digits,
    formatter = formatter,
    ...
  )
}

# Recover the season-weighted centering/scaling constants used to back-transform t0.
weighted_date_scaling <- function(data, date_col = "date_J") {
  if (all(c("date_J_mean_ref", "date_J_sd_ref") %in% names(data))) {
    date_stats <- data %>%
      group_by(season) %>%
      summarise(
        mean_value = first(date_J_mean_ref),
        sd_value = first(date_J_sd_ref),
        n = dplyr::n(),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  } else {
    date_stats <- data %>%
      group_by(season) %>%
      summarise(
        mean_value = mean(.data[[date_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
        sd_value = sd(.data[[date_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
        n = dplyr::n(),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  }

  tibble(
    weighted_mean = weighted.mean(date_stats$mean_value, w = date_stats$n, na.rm = TRUE),
    weighted_sd = weighted.mean(date_stats$sd_value, w = date_stats$n, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

find_posterior_draw_col <- function(post, patterns, description) {
  col_name <- names(post)[Reduce(`&`, lapply(patterns, grepl, x = names(post)))]

  if (length(col_name) != 1) {
    stop("Could not identify posterior draw column for ", description, ".")
  }

  col_name
}

find_posterior_draw_col_by_terms <- function(post, include_terms, description,
                                             exclude_terms = character()) {
  col_names <- names(post)[grepl("^b_t0_", names(post))]
  keep_include <- Reduce(
    `&`,
    lapply(include_terms, function(term) grepl(term, col_names, fixed = TRUE))
  )

  if (length(exclude_terms) > 0) {
    keep_exclude <- Reduce(
      `|`,
      lapply(exclude_terms, function(term) grepl(term, col_names, fixed = TRUE))
    )
  } else {
    keep_exclude <- rep(FALSE, length(col_names))
  }

  col_name <- col_names[keep_include & !keep_exclude]

  if (length(col_name) != 1) {
    stop("Could not identify posterior draw column for ", description, ".")
  }

  col_name
}




# Convert `performance::r2_bayes()` output into the same table-ready format used elsewhere.
summarise_bayes_r2 <- function(fitted_model) {
  r2_df <- performance::r2_bayes(fitted_model) %>% as.data.frame()

  tibble(
    parameter = c("Marginal R²", "Conditional R²"),
    median = c(r2_df$R2[2], r2_df$R2[1]),
    ci_lower = c(r2_df$CI_low[2], r2_df$CI_low[1]),
    ci_upper = c(r2_df$CI_high[2], r2_df$CI_high[1])
  )
}

# Add repeatability- and variance-related draws used in the sex-only summary table.
add_repeatability_draws <- function(post) {
  post %>%
    mutate(
      var_baseline_rings_comb = sd_rings_comb__baseline_Intercept^2,
      var_t0_rings_comb = sd_rings_comb__t0_Intercept^2,
      var_baseline_rings_comb_season =
        `sd_rings_comb:season__baseline_Intercept`^2,
      var_t0_rings_comb_season =
        `sd_rings_comb:season__t0_Intercept`^2,
      var_baseline_total =
        var_baseline_rings_comb + var_baseline_rings_comb_season,
      var_t0_total =
        var_t0_rings_comb + var_t0_rings_comb_season,
      # Parameter-level repeatability uses each latent parameter's own
      # bird and bird-season variances. Score residual variance belongs to
      # the observation model and must not be added to date variance.
      R_baseline_between_year = var_baseline_rings_comb / var_baseline_total,
      R_t0_between_year = var_t0_rings_comb / var_t0_total,
      R_baseline_minus_t0 = R_baseline_between_year - R_t0_between_year,
      cor_baseline_t0 = cor_rings_comb__baseline_Intercept__t0_Intercept,
      resid_var = sigma^2
    )
}

get_model_season_levels <- function(model_obj) {
  if (!"season" %in% names(model_obj$data)) {
    return(character())
  }

  if (is.factor(model_obj$data$season)) {
    levels(droplevels(model_obj$data$season))
  } else {
    sort(unique(as.character(model_obj$data$season)))
  }
}

has_t0_season_effect <- function(post) {
  any(grepl("^b_t0_season", names(post)))
}

extract_t0_season_draws <- function(model_obj, post = NULL) {
  if (is.null(post)) {
    post <- as_draws_df(model_obj$fitted_model)
  }

  season_levels <- get_model_season_levels(model_obj)

  if (length(season_levels) == 0) {
    return(list())
  }

  season_stats <- model_obj$data %>%
    select(any_of(c("season", "date_J_mean_ref", "date_J_sd_ref"))) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    mutate(season = as.character(season))

  if (!all(c("date_J_mean_ref", "date_J_sd_ref") %in% names(season_stats))) {
    season_stats <- date_scaling_ref %>%
      filter(season %in% season_levels) %>%
      mutate(season = as.character(season))
  }

  setNames(lapply(season_levels, function(season_i) {
    season_coef_name <- paste0("b_t0_season", season_i)
    season_draws <- post$b_t0_Intercept

    if (season_coef_name %in% names(post)) {
      season_draws <- season_draws + post[[season_coef_name]]
    }

    season_ref <- season_stats %>%
      filter(season == season_i)

    season_draws * season_ref$date_J_sd_ref + season_ref$date_J_mean_ref
  }), season_levels)
}

season_t0_parameter_names <- function(model_obj) {
  season_levels <- get_model_season_levels(model_obj)

  if (length(season_levels) < 2) {
    return(character())
  }

  c(
    paste0(
      "Pre-basic moult midpoint (t0), season ",
      season_levels,
      ", females (reference)"
    ),
    vapply(combn(season_levels, 2, simplify = FALSE), function(season_pair) {
      paste0(
        "Season effect on pre-basic moult midpoint (t0): ",
        season_pair[[2]],
        " - ",
        season_pair[[1]]
      )
    }, character(1))
  )
}

summarise_t0_season_effects <- function(
    model_obj,
    type = "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    parameter_group = "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)") {
  post <- as_draws_df(model_obj$fitted_model)

  if (!has_t0_season_effect(post)) {
    return(tibble())
  }

  season_draws <- extract_t0_season_draws(model_obj, post)
  season_levels <- names(season_draws)
  season_pairs <- combn(season_levels, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  bind_rows(
    bind_rows(lapply(season_levels, function(season_i) {
      summary_row(
        paste0(
          "Pre-basic moult midpoint (t0), season ",
          season_i,
          ", females (reference)"
        ),
        type,
        parameter_group,
        season_draws[[season_i]],
        formatter = format_shifted_julian_interval
      )
    })),
    bind_rows(lapply(season_pairs, function(season_pair) {
      summary_row(
        paste0(
          "Season effect on pre-basic moult midpoint (t0): ",
          season_pair[[2]],
          " - ",
          season_pair[[1]]
        ),
        type,
        parameter_group,
        season_draws[[season_pair[[2]]]] - season_draws[[season_pair[[1]]]]
      )
    }))
  )
}

pick_parameter_rows <- function(tbl, parameters) {
  tbl %>%
    mutate(.order = match(parameter, parameters)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(.order)) %>%
    arrange(.order) %>%
    select(-.order)
}

# Keep the HTML diagnostics compact by reducing each fitted model to a few convergence checks.
model_diagnostics_table <- function(model_list) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(model_list, function(model_obj, model_name) {
    draw_summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(
      posterior::as_draws_array(model_obj$fitted_model),
      "rhat",
      "ess_bulk",
      "ess_tail"
    )

    sampler <- brms::nuts_params(model_obj$fitted_model)
    tibble(
      model = model_name,
      max_rhat = round(max(draw_summary$rhat, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
      n_rhat_over_1_01 = sum(draw_summary$rhat > 1.01, na.rm = TRUE),
      min_bulk_ess = floor(min(draw_summary$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE)),
      min_tail_ess = floor(min(draw_summary$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE)),
      n_divergent = sum(sampler$Value[sampler$Parameter == "divergent__"]),
      tree_depth_limit_hits = sum(sampler$Value[sampler$Parameter == "treedepth__"] >= 15)
    )
  })
}

# Use the same simple table style across the Results section.
display_result_table <- function(tbl) {
  tbl %>%
    select(parameter, median_CI) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      parameter = "Parameter",
      median_CI = gt::md("Posterior median [95% CrI]")
    ) %>%
    cols_align(align = "left", columns = everything())
}

display_consolidated_table <- function(tbl) {
  count_model_individuals <- function(obj_name, fallback) {
    if (exists(obj_name, inherits = TRUE)) {
      obj <- get(obj_name, inherits = TRUE)
      if (is.list(obj) && "data" %in% names(obj) && "rings_comb" %in% names(obj$data)) {
        return(dplyr::n_distinct(obj$data$rings_comb))
      }
    }

    fallback
  }

  format_num <- function(x, digits = 2) {
    out <- format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)
    out <- sub("(?<=\\d)0+$", "", out, perl = TRUE)
    out <- sub("\\.$", "", out)
    out <- sub("^-0$", "0", out)
    out
  }

  format_date_median <- function(x, origin_year = 2021) {
    sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(x, origin_year), "%d %b"))
  }

  format_date_ci <- function(lo, hi, origin_year = 2021) {
    paste0(
      "[",
      sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(lo, origin_year), "%d %b")),
      ", ",
      sub("^0", "", format(shifted_julian_to_date(hi, origin_year), "%d %b")),
      "]"
    )
  }

  n_lookup <- c(
    "Sex-specific" = count_model_individuals("sex_mod", 100L),
    "Age-class" = count_model_individuals("sex_age_class_mod", 83L),
    "Migratory status" = count_model_individuals("sex_migratory_status_mod", 41L)
  )

  section_levels <- c(
    "Fixed effects on baseline breeding plumage score (β)",
    "Fixed effects on post-breeding molt midpoint (t0): season, sex, age-class, and migration strategy",
    "Derived days per score at midpoint",
    "Repeatability of molt traits (R)",
    "Model fit",
    "Variance components and residual structure"
  )

  display_tbl <- tbl %>%
    mutate(
      section = case_when(
        grepl("days per score at midpoint", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
          "Derived days per score at midpoint",
        type == "Repeatability" ~ "Repeatability of molt traits (R)",
        type == "Model-level goodness-of-fit" ~ "Model fit",
        type %in% c(
          "Between-individual variance (random effects)",
          "Bird-season variance (random effects)",
          "Random-effects correlation",
          "Residual (within-observation) variance"
        ) ~ "Variance components and residual structure",
        grepl("baseline alternate plumage score", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
          "Fixed effects on baseline breeding plumage score (β)",
        grepl("moult mid", parameter, ignore.case = TRUE) ~
          "Fixed effects on post-breeding molt midpoint (t0): season, sex, age-class, and migration strategy",
        TRUE ~ type
      ),
      row_label = case_when(
        grepl("^Baseline alternate plumage score.*females", parameter) ~
          "Intercept, females (reference; score)",
        grepl("^Sex effect on baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Sex effect (males – females; Δ score)",
        grepl("^Age-class effect on baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Age-class effect (AFY – FY; Δ score)",
        grepl("^Migratory-strategy effect on baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Migratory-strategy effect (Resident – Migrant; Δ score)",
        grepl("^Pre-basic moult midpoint \\(t0\\), season", parameter) ~
          paste0(
            "Season ",
            paste0(stringr::str_extract(parameter, "\\d{4}"), "–",
                   as.integer(stringr::str_extract(parameter, "\\d{4}")) + 1L),
            " midpoint, females (reference; date)"
          ),
        grepl("^Pre-basic moult midpoint.*females", parameter) ~
          "Intercept, females (reference; date)",
        grepl("^Season effect on pre-basic moult midpoint", parameter) ~
          paste0(
            "Season effect (",
            stringr::str_replace_all(
              stringr::str_match(parameter, "t0\\): (.*)$")[, 2],
              "202[123]", function(year) paste0(year, "–", as.integer(year) + 1L)),
            "; Δ days)"
          ),
        grepl("^Sex effect on pre-basic moult mid", parameter) ~
          "Sex effect (males – females; Δ days)",
        grepl("^Age-class effect on pre-basic moult", parameter) ~
          "Age-class effect (AFY – FY; Δ days)",
        grepl("^Migratory-strategy effect on pre-basic moult midpoint", parameter) ~
          "Migratory-strategy effect (Resident – Migrant; Δ days)",
        grepl("^Derived days per score at midpoint.*females", parameter) ~
          "Intercept, females (reference; days·score⁻¹)",
        grepl("^Sex contrast in derived days per score at midpoint", parameter) ~
          "Sex effect (males – females; days·score⁻¹)",
        parameter == "Between-year repeatability of alternate plumage" ~
          "Between-year repeatability of β",
        parameter == "Within-year repeatability of alternate plumage" ~
          "Within-year repeatability of β",
        parameter == "Between-year repeatability of pre-basic moult mid-point date" ~
          "Between-year repeatability of t0",
        parameter == "Within-year repeatability of pre-basic moult mid-point date" ~
          "Within-year repeatability of t0",
        parameter == "Between-individual variance in baseline plumage score" ~
          "Between-individual variance in β",
        parameter == "Between-individual variance in pre-basic moult midpoint date" ~
          "Between-individual variance in t0",
        parameter == "Bird-season variance in baseline plumage score" ~
          "Bird-season variance in β",
        parameter == "Bird-season variance in pre-basic moult midpoint date" ~
          "Bird-season variance in t0",
        grepl("^Correlation between baseline alternate plumage score", parameter) ~
          "Correlation between β and t0",
        TRUE ~ parameter
      ),
      model = case_when(
        grepl("^Age-class effect", parameter) ~ "Age-class",
        grepl("^Migratory-strategy effect", parameter) ~ "Migratory status",
        TRUE ~ "Sex-specific"
      ),
      n_ind = as.integer(unname(n_lookup[model])),
      posterior_median = if_else(
        grepl("^Pre-basic moult midpoint.*females", parameter),
        format_date_median(estimate),
        format_num(estimate)
      ),
      credible_interval = if_else(
        grepl("^Pre-basic moult midpoint.*females", parameter),
        format_date_ci(ci_lower, ci_upper),
        paste0("[", format_num(ci_lower), ", ", format_num(ci_upper), "]")
      ),
      section = factor(section, levels = section_levels)
    ) %>%
    select(section, row_label, posterior_median, credible_interval, n_ind, model)

  display_tbl %>%
    gt::gt(groupname_col = "section", rowname_col = "row_label") %>%
    gt::tab_stubhead(label = "") %>%
    gt::cols_label(
      posterior_median = "Posterior median",
      credible_interval = "[95% CrI]",
      n_ind = gt::html("N<sub>ind</sub>"),
      model = "Model"
    ) %>%
    gt::cols_align(
      align = "center",
      columns = c(posterior_median, credible_interval, n_ind)
    ) %>%
    gt::cols_align(align = "left", columns = model) %>%
    gt::cols_width(
      gt::stub() ~ gt::px(360),
      posterior_median ~ gt::px(115),
      credible_interval ~ gt::px(150),
      n_ind ~ gt::px(60),
      model ~ gt::px(150)
    ) %>%
    gt::tab_style(
      style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = gt::cells_row_groups()
    ) %>%
    gt::tab_style(
      style = gt::cell_borders(sides = "top", color = "black", weight = gt::px(1)),
      locations = gt::cells_row_groups()
    ) %>%
    gt::tab_options(
      table.width = gt::pct(100),
      table.font.size = gt::px(12),
      data_row.padding = gt::px(3),
      row_group.padding = gt::px(4),
      source_notes.font.size = gt::px(11)
    ) %>%
    gt::tab_source_note(
      source_note = gt::md(
        "Note: Δ denotes an additive difference relative to the reference category (for categorical predictors) or the expected change in the response per unit change in the predictor (for continuous covariates)."
      )
    )
}
```

```{r results-load-models, echo=TRUE}
# Load each saved model once so the visible chunks can stay short and readable.
sex_mod <- readRDS(here("out/sex_mod_.rds"))
sex_age_class_mod <- readRDS(here("out/sex_age_class_mod_2.rds"))
sex_migratory_status_mod <- readRDS(here("out/sex_migratory_status_mod_.rds"))

results_models <- list(
  "Sex + season moult model" = sex_mod,
  "Sex + season + age-class model" = sex_age_class_mod,
  "Sex + season + migratory-status model" = sex_migratory_status_mod
)

```

#### Diagnostics
We checked convergence using R-hat, effective sample sizes and sampler diagnostics. The tables summarize the saved fits.
```{r results-diagnostics, echo=FALSE}
diagnostics_table <- model_diagnostics_table(results_models)

diagnostics_table %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    model = "Model",
    max_rhat = "Max R-hat",
    n_rhat_over_1_01 = "Parameters with R-hat > 1.01",
    min_bulk_ess = "Min bulk ESS",
    min_tail_ess = "Min tail ESS",
    n_divergent = "Divergent transitions",
    tree_depth_limit_hits = "Tree-depth-limit hits"
  )
```

### Results: Sex-specific model
We use the sex model as the main reference because it uses the full dataset. It shows clear sex differences in baseline ornament expression, clear season-to-season shifts in molt midpoint, no clear sex difference in midpoint, and strong repeatability in baseline ornament expression but limited between-year repeatability in timing.

```{r results-sex-model, echo=TRUE}
# Start from the saved posterior draws so this chunk reproduces the reported table without refitting.
sex_post <- as_draws_df(sex_mod$fitted_model)

# Use season-weighted centering/scaling constants to convert the model's t0 estimate back to days.
date_scale <- weighted_date_scaling(sex_mod$data)
mean_date_sd <- date_scale$weighted_sd
mean_date_mean <- date_scale$weighted_mean

# Derive the biological quantities reported in the consolidated table.
sex_post <- sex_post %>%
  mutate(
    baseline_sexF = b_baseline_Intercept,
    baseline_sexM = b_baseline_Intercept + b_baseline_sexM,
    baseline_sex_diff = b_baseline_sexM,
    t0_sexF = b_t0_Intercept * mean_date_sd + mean_date_mean,
    t0_sex_diff = b_t0_sexM * mean_date_sd,
    rate_days_score_sexF = 1 / (((baseline_sexF - 1) * b_k_Intercept) / (4 * mean_date_sd)),
    rate_days_score_sexM = 1 / (((baseline_sexM - 1) * b_k_Intercept) / (4 * mean_date_sd)),
    rate_days_score_diff = rate_days_score_sexM - rate_days_score_sexF
  ) %>%
  add_repeatability_draws()

# Bayesian R² is already summarised, so convert it directly into table rows.
sex_r2 <- summarise_bayes_r2(sex_mod$fitted_model)
sex_t0_rows <- if (has_t0_season_effect(sex_post)) {
  bind_rows(
    summarise_t0_season_effects(sex_mod),
    summary_row(
      "Sex effect on pre-basic moult midpoint (t0): males − females",
      "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
      "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)",
      sex_post$t0_sex_diff
    )
  )
} else {
  bind_rows(
    summary_row(
      "Pre-basic moult midpoint (t0), females (reference)",
      "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
      "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)",
      sex_post$t0_sexF,
      formatter = format_shifted_julian_interval
    ),
    summary_row(
      "Sex effect on pre-basic moult midpoint (t0): males − females",
      "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
      "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)",
      sex_post$t0_sex_diff
    )
  )
}

sex_mod_summary_table <- bind_rows(
  summary_row(
    "Baseline alternate plumage score (β), females (reference)",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Full alternate plumage score (beta)",
    sex_post$baseline_sexF
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Sex effect on baseline alternate plumage score (β): males − females",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Full alternate plumage score (beta)",
    sex_post$baseline_sex_diff
  ),
  sex_t0_rows,
  summary_row(
    "Derived days per score at midpoint (days·score⁻¹), females (reference)",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Derived days per score (shared k)",
    sex_post$rate_days_score_sexF
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Sex contrast in derived days per score at midpoint (days·score⁻¹): males − females",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Derived days per score (shared k)",
    sex_post$rate_days_score_diff
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Between-year repeatability of alternate plumage",
    "Repeatability",
    "",
    sex_post$R_baseline_between_year
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Between-year repeatability of pre-basic moult mid-point date",
    "Repeatability",
    "",
    sex_post$R_t0_between_year
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Baseline minus midpoint repeatability",
    "Repeatability", "", sex_post$R_baseline_minus_t0
  ),
  summary_row_from_stats(
    "Marginal R²",
    "Model-level goodness-of-fit",
    "",
    sex_r2 %>% slice(1)
  ),
  summary_row_from_stats(
    "Conditional R²",
    "Model-level goodness-of-fit",
    "",
    sex_r2 %>% slice(2)
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Between-individual variance in baseline plumage score",
    "Between-individual variance (random effects)",
    "",
    sex_post$var_baseline_rings_comb
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Between-individual variance in pre-basic moult midpoint date",
    "Between-individual variance (random effects)",
    "",
    sex_post$var_t0_rings_comb
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Bird-season variance in baseline plumage score",
    "Bird-season variance (random effects)", "",
    sex_post$var_baseline_rings_comb_season
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Bird-season variance in pre-basic moult midpoint date",
    "Bird-season variance (random effects)", "",
    sex_post$var_t0_rings_comb_season
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Correlation between baseline alternate plumage score and pre-basic moult midpoint date",
    "Random-effects correlation",
    "",
    sex_post$cor_baseline_t0
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Residual variance",
    "Residual (within-observation) variance",
    "",
    sex_post$resid_var
  )
)

display_result_table(sex_mod_summary_table)
```


Adjusted repeatability describes the persistence of individual differences in baseline and midpoint after controlling for each parameter's fixed effects. The ratios use bird variance divided by bird plus bird-season variance. Photographic-score residual variance is excluded. These estimates do not directly measure responses to changes in breeding phenology or reproductive state.

### Results: Age Class model
The age-class model showed a clear contrast between first-year and after-first-year birds, driven mainly by later molt midpoints in older birds. There was no clear difference between age classes in baseline plumage score.

```{r results-age-class-model, echo=TRUE}
age_class_post <- as_draws_df(sex_age_class_mod$fitted_model)

# Convert the age-class t0 effect from scaled units back to days.
date_scale <- weighted_date_scaling(sex_age_class_mod$data)
mean_date_sd <- date_scale$weighted_sd

sex_age_class_mod_summary_table <- bind_rows(
  summary_row(
    "Age-class effect on baseline alternate plumage score (β): AFY − FY",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Full alternate plumage score (beta)",
    age_class_post$b_baseline_age_classAFY
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Age-class effect on pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0): AFY − FY",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)",
    age_class_post$b_t0_age_classAFY * mean_date_sd
  )
)

display_result_table(sex_age_class_mod_summary_table)
```

### Results: Migratory Strategy model
We found no clear difference between residents and migrants in baseline expression or molt midpoint. The broad credible intervals do not establish equivalent schedules.

```{r results-migratory-model, echo=TRUE}
# The consolidated table only reports the migratory-status contrasts, so keep this chunk to those rows.
migratory_post <- as_draws_df(sex_migratory_status_mod$fitted_model)

# Convert the migratory-status effect on t0 from scaled units back to days.
date_scale <- weighted_date_scaling(sex_migratory_status_mod$data)
mean_date_sd <- date_scale$weighted_sd

sex_migratory_status_mod_summary_table <- bind_rows(
  summary_row(
    "Migratory-strategy effect on baseline alternate plumage score (β): Resident − Migrant",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Full alternate plumage score (beta)",
    migratory_post$b_baseline_migratory_statusR
  ),
  summary_row(
    "Migratory-strategy effect on pre-basic moult midpoint (t0): Resident − Migrant",
    "Posterior estimates (state-specific means)",
    "Pre-basic moult mid-point date (t0)",
    migratory_post$b_t0_migratory_statusR * mean_date_sd
  )
)

display_result_table(sex_migratory_status_mod_summary_table)
```

### Table 1 {#table-1}
State-specific, season and repeatability results. Values are posterior medians and 95% credible intervals. Variance components remain on the fitted parameter scales. Derived days per score depend on baseline and the shared $k$ and do not test state-specific variation in steepness.

### Results: Breeding schedules and molt midpoint {#afy-breeding-models}

The three main breeding–molt models are restricted to confidently after-first-year (AFY)
bird-seasons. They contain 1,045 scored observations from 47 after-first-year birds across
86 bird-seasons. Twenty-eight birds contributed repeated seasons, including
17 with two and 11 with three. We calculated each bird's mean breeding date
and seasonal deviation from one record per retained bird-season after the
AFY restriction. The breeding dates retain their original centering within
season. Both components predict molt midpoint, while baseline retains sex
and random effects. The models use the same priors, shared transition
steepness and four chains of 10,000 iterations (5,000 warmup) as the main
models. They estimate a common within-individual slope, not individual
reaction-norm slopes. Single-season birds have a zero within-individual
deviation and contribute to the among-individual comparison.

#### R implementation of equations (6) and (7)

The common complete-case sample requires all three breeding-date predictors. Each predictor is then fitted separately. The code below follows the existing fitting script and retains its data filtering, factor levels, priors and random effects.

```{r afy-data-construction}
predictors <- c("first_breeding_date_J_snum", "last_nest_first_obs_J_snum",
                "last_breeding_date_J_snum")
dat_afy <- dat_breeding %>%
  filter(age_class == "AFY") %>%
  select(score, date_J, rings_comb, sex, season, age_class, age_class_source,
         all_of(predictors)) %>% distinct() %>%
  add_reference_date_scaling() %>%
  drop_na(score, date_J, sex, rings_comb, season, all_of(predictors)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(rings_comb, sex, season, age_class, age_class_source),
                ~ if (is.factor(.x)) droplevels(.x) else factor(.x))) %>%
  as.data.frame()
bird_seasons <- distinct(dat_afy, rings_comb, season)

build_afy_dataset <- function(predictor) {
  phenology <- dat_afy %>%
    select(rings_comb, season, all_of(predictor)) %>% distinct()
  stopifnot(nrow(phenology) == nrow(bird_seasons))
  phenology <- phenology %>% group_by(rings_comb) %>%
    mutate(n_phenology_seasons = n(),
           breeding_mean_i = mean(.data[[predictor]]),
           breeding_dev_is = .data[[predictor]] - breeding_mean_i) %>% ungroup()
  checks <- phenology %>% group_by(rings_comb) %>%
    summarise(mean_deviation = mean(breeding_dev_is), .groups = "drop")
  stopifnot(max(abs(checks$mean_deviation)) < 1e-10)
  dat_afy %>% left_join(phenology, by = c("rings_comb", "season", predictor)) %>%
    as.data.frame()
}

afy_formula <- bf(
  score ~ 1 + (baseline - 1) * (1 - 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (date_J_scaled - t0)))),
  baseline ~ sex + (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  t0 ~ sex + season + breeding_mean_i + breeding_dev_is +
    (1 | i | rings_comb) + (1 | rings_comb:season),
  k ~ 1, nl = TRUE
)
```

```{r afy-optional-fit, eval=FALSE}
# Fit each predictor separately with the same priors defined above.
# Use seeds 261, 262 and 263 for first date, last nest and last date, respectively.
dat_afy_last <- build_afy_dataset("last_breeding_date_J_snum")
fit_afy_last <- brm(
  formula = afy_formula, data = dat_afy_last,
  family = gaussian(), prior = moult_priors,
  chains = 4, cores = 4, iter = 10000, warmup = 5000,
  backend = "cmdstanr", seed = 263,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 15)
)
# The existing script fits all three predictors and saves the reporting scale,
# model data and session information alongside each completed fit.
# Run it manually only when a full refit is intended:
# source(here("scripts/run_afy_within_individual_breeding_phenology_models.R"))
```

```{r afy-results-load-and-summarise, echo=TRUE, results="hide"}
afy_specs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~label, ~path,
  "First observed breeding date", "sex_first_breed_within_individual_afy_mod_.rds",
  "Last nest date", "sex_last_nest_within_individual_afy_mod_.rds",
  "Last observed breeding date", "sex_last_breed_within_individual_afy_mod_.rds"
)
afy_models <- setNames(lapply(afy_specs$path, function(x) readRDS(here("out", x))),
                       afy_specs$label)
afy_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(afy_models), function(label_i) {
  model_i <- afy_models[[label_i]]
  stopifnot(nrow(model_i$data) == 1045,
            n_distinct(model_i$data$rings_comb) == 47,
            nrow(distinct(model_i$data, rings_comb, season)) == 86,
            all(model_i$data$age_class == "AFY"))
  rebuilt_i <- build_afy_dataset(model_i$predictor)
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(model_i$data, rebuilt_i)))
  draws_i <- as_draws_df(model_i$fitted_model)
  sd_days_i <- model_i$midpoint_days_conversion
  among_i <- draws_i$b_t0_breeding_mean_i * sd_days_i
  within_i <- draws_i$b_t0_breeding_dev_is * sd_days_i
  bind_rows(lapply(c("Among individuals", "Within individuals", "Among minus within"),
    function(component_i) {
      values_i <- switch(component_i,
                         "Among individuals" = among_i,
                         "Within individuals" = within_i,
                         "Among minus within" = among_i - within_i)
      summarise_posterior(values_i) %>%
        mutate(predictor = label_i, component = component_i)
    }))
}))
write.csv(afy_summary, here("out", "revision3_afy_table2.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

**Table 2.** Among- and within-individual associations between breeding schedules and molt midpoint in after-first-year birds.
Values are days of midpoint delay per one-day breeding-date delay.
Among minus within is calculated from paired posterior draws and directly
compares the two slopes. The last nest date combines estimated laying dates
and first observations, as defined in the manuscript Methods.

```{r afy-table2, echo=TRUE}
afy_table2 <- afy_summary %>%
  mutate(value = format_numeric_interval(select(., median, ci_lower, ci_upper))) %>%
  select(`Breeding date` = predictor, component, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = component, values_from = value) %>%
  arrange(match(`Breeding date`, afy_specs$label))
knitr::kable(afy_table2)
```

For last observed breeding date, the among-individual estimate is positive,
but there is no clear within-individual association. The same pattern occurs
for last nest date. The direct among-minus-within contrast excludes zero
for last nest date, but not for last observed breeding date. Neither
component is clearly associated with first observed breeding date. These
results do not demonstrate an absence of individual plasticity.

```{r afy-diagnostics, echo=FALSE}
afy_diagnostics <- model_diagnostics_table(afy_models)
afy_diagnostics$n_divergent <- vapply(afy_models, function(model_i) {
  np <- brms::nuts_params(model_i$fitted_model)
  sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "divergent__"])
}, numeric(1))
afy_diagnostics %>% knitr::kable()
write.csv(afy_diagnostics, here("out", "revision3_afy_diagnostics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#### breeding histograms
# 1) Get per-season centering/scaling constants from the ORIGINAL (unscaled) shifted-Julian variables
stats <- breeding_data_all %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(
    mu_last  = mean(last_breeding_date_J, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_last  = sd(last_breeding_date_J,  na.rm = TRUE),
    mu_first = mean(first_breeding_date_J, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_first = sd(first_breeding_date_J,  na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2) Join constants, invert transform, then convert shifted-Julian (1 = Jul 1) to a common calendar date
ref_start <- as.Date("2001-07-01")  # any non-leap year works well

  distinct(rings_comb, season,
           last_breeding_date_J_snum,

  mutate(
    # If _snum is CENTER-ONLY (scale = 0): x = centered + mean
    last_J  = last_breeding_date_J_snum  + mu_last,
    first_J = first_breeding_date_J_snum + mu_first,

    # Convert shifted-Julian to a common calendar date (same year for all seasons)
    last_date_common  = ref_start + round(last_J  - 1),
    first_date_common = ref_start + round(first_J - 1),

    # Optional: month-day labels (often what you want for plotting)
    last_md  = format(last_date_common,  "%b-%d"),
    first_md = format(first_date_common, "%b-%d")
```

### Figure 3 — state-specific molt trajectories {#figure-3}
This figure reproduces the manuscript's state-dependent summary of the sex,
age-class, and migratory-strategy models. The left column shows population-level
predicted molt trajectories, while the middle and right columns show the
state-specific posteriors for molt midpoint (`t0`) and the baseline rufous-band
score (`β`).

```{r figure3-display, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.8, out.width="100%"}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show code for Figure 3"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig-dpi: 300
#| out-width: "8in"
combined_origin <- as.Date("2021-07-01")
combined_curve_limits <- c(as.Date("2021-07-20"), as.Date("2022-05-04"))
combined_curve_breaks <- seq(
  from = as.Date("2021-07-27"),
  to = as.Date("2022-04-12"),
  by = "4 weeks"
)
combined_t0_limits <- c(160, 250)
combined_t0_breaks <- seq(174, 300, by = 21)
combined_t0_visible_breaks <- combined_t0_breaks[
  combined_t0_breaks >= combined_t0_limits[1] &
    combined_t0_breaks <= combined_t0_limits[2]
]
combined_baseline_breaks <- 4:7
combined_baseline_break_scale <-
  diff(range(combined_baseline_breaks)) / diff(range(combined_t0_visible_breaks))
combined_baseline_limits <- c(
  combined_baseline_breaks[1] -
    (combined_t0_visible_breaks[1] - combined_t0_limits[1]) *
      combined_baseline_break_scale,
  combined_baseline_breaks[length(combined_baseline_breaks)] +
    (combined_t0_limits[2] - tail(combined_t0_visible_breaks, 1)) *
      combined_baseline_break_scale
)
nest_period_start <- min(found_dates_all_$date_)
nest_period_end <- max(found_dates_all_$date_)

combined_jday_to_label <- function(x) {
  format(combined_origin + round(x) - 1, "%d %b")
}

make_plot_date_lookup <- function(model_obj) {
  dat_plot <- model_obj$data
  n_dates <- max(dat_plot$date_J) - min(dat_plot$date_J) + 1

  tibble(
    date_J = seq(
      from = min(dat_plot$date_J),
      to = max(dat_plot$date_J),
      length.out = n_dates
    ),
    date_J_scaled = seq(
      from = min(dat_plot$date_J_scaled),
      to = max(dat_plot$date_J_scaled),
      length.out = n_dates
    )
  ) %>%
    mutate(date_ = combined_origin + round(date_J - 1))
}

make_population_predictions <- function(model_obj, state_grid) {
  date_lookup <- make_plot_date_lookup(model_obj)

  newdata <- tidyr::crossing(
    date_J_scaled = date_lookup$date_J_scaled,
    state_grid
  ) %>%
    mutate(rings_comb = NA, season = NA) %>%
    left_join(date_lookup, by = "date_J_scaled")

  fitted_vals <- fitted(
    model_obj$fitted_model,
    newdata = newdata,
    re_formula = NA,
    summary = TRUE
  )

  newdata %>%
    mutate(
      fit = fitted_vals[, "Estimate"],
      lower = fitted_vals[, "Q2.5"],
      upper = fitted_vals[, "Q97.5"]
    )
}

make_individual_predictions <- function(model_obj, id_cols, ndraws = 50) {
  date_lookup <- make_plot_date_lookup(model_obj)

  newdata <- tidyr::crossing(
    date_J_scaled = date_lookup$date_J_scaled,
    model_obj$data %>% distinct(across(all_of(id_cols)))
  )

  add_epred_draws(
    model_obj$fitted_model,
    newdata = newdata,
    ndraws = ndraws
  ) %>%
    left_join(date_lookup, by = "date_J_scaled")
}

curve_panel_theme <- function(show_x = FALSE, bottom_margin = 5.5) {
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    text = element_text(family = "sans"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey30", face = "italic"),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11, colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "cm"),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, lineend = "round", colour = "grey90"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, lineend = "round", colour = "grey60"),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = if (show_x) {
      element_text(size = 9, angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, colour = "grey30")
    } else {
      element_blank()
    },
    plot.margin = unit(c(0, -15, bottom_margin, 0), "pt")
  )
}

posterior_panel_theme <- function(show_x = FALSE, bottom_margin = 0) {
  theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey40"),
      axis.title.x = if (show_x) {
        element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey40")
      } else {
        element_blank()
      },
      axis.text.x = if (show_x) {
        element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey40", angle = 45, hjust = 1)
      } else {
        element_blank()
      },
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      text = element_text(family = "sans"),
      plot.margin = margin(0, 5.5, bottom_margin, 10)
    )
}

count_individuals_by_state <- function(model_obj, state_col) {
  model_obj$data %>%
    distinct(rings_comb, .data[[state_col]]) %>%
    count(.data[[state_col]], name = "n_ind")
}

make_state_labeler <- function(label_map) {
  function(x) unname(label_map[x])
}

make_halfeye_plot <- function(draws_tbl,
                              fill_values,
                              x_limits,
                              x_breaks,
                              x_title_font = FALSE,
                              x_labels = waiver(),
                              x_title = NULL,
                              show_x = FALSE,
                              state_labels = waiver(),
                              show_y_labels = TRUE,
                              point_shape = 23,
                              bottom_margin = 0) {
  ggplot(draws_tbl, aes(x = estimate, y = state, fill = state)) +
    stat_halfeye(
      .width = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95),
      color = "black",
      point_fill = "white",
      shape = point_shape,
      slab_alpha = 0.75
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(
      limits = rev(names(fill_values)),
      labels = state_labels
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_values) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = x_limits,
      breaks = x_breaks,
      labels = x_labels,
      expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
    ) +
    labs(x = x_title) +
    posterior_panel_theme(show_x = show_x, bottom_margin = bottom_margin) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = if (show_y_labels) {
        element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey40")
      } else {
        element_blank()
      },
      axis.title.x =
        if (x_title_font == "ggtext") {
          ggtext::element_markdown(family = "sans")
        } else if (x_title_font == "normal") {
          element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey40")
        } else if (x_title_font == "none") {
          element_blank()
        }
	    )
	}

make_sex_dodged_baseline_plot <- function(draws_tbl,
                                          state_levels,
                                          fill_values,
                                          x_limits,
                                          x_breaks,
                                          x_title = NULL,
                                          show_x = FALSE,
                                          x_title_font = FALSE,
                                          show_y_labels = FALSE,
                                          bottom_margin = 0) {
  ggplot(
    draws_tbl %>%
      mutate(
        sex = factor(sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
        state = factor(state, levels = state_levels)
      ),
    aes(x = estimate, y = state, fill = state, group = interaction(state, sex))
  ) +
    stat_halfeye(
      .width = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95),
      color = "black",
      point_fill = "white",
      shape = 21,
      slab_alpha = 0.75,
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(state_levels)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_values) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = x_limits,
      breaks = x_breaks,
      expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(
      ylim = c(0.4, length(state_levels) + 1),
      expand = FALSE,
      clip = "off"
    ) +
    labs(x = x_title) +
    posterior_panel_theme(show_x = show_x, bottom_margin = bottom_margin) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = if (show_y_labels) {
        element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey40")
      } else {
        element_blank()
      },
      axis.title.x =
        if (x_title_font == "ggtext") {
          ggtext::element_markdown(family = "sans")
        } else if (x_title_font == "normal") {
          element_text(size = 11, colour = "grey40")
        } else if (x_title_font == "none") {
          element_blank()
        }
    )
}
```

**Figure 3.** State-specific molt trajectories. (a) Predicted post-breeding molt schedules from the sex, age-class and migratory-status models. Ribbons show 95% credible intervals for population trajectories, and faint lines show selected posterior draws for individual bird-seasons. Gray shading denotes the nest-observation period. The posterior distributions describe (b) molt midpoint and (c) baseline expression. Age-class and migration midpoint distributions use females as the reference sex. Panel (c) shows baseline distributions separately for females and males. White symbols indicate posterior medians, and black bars show 50%, 80% and 95% credible intervals.
